text:
Ravi (oncall): Passing off to morning crew — quick summary of what happened overnight. TL;DR: embeddings-router returned intermittent 503s for ~15m. Autoscaler oscillation + a single worker OOM during a GC pause were the proximate causes. I mitigated with a scaled-up pool and pinned the quantized fallback model; errors dropped back to baseline.

incident-bot: Pager #4302 triggered at 2026-03-14T03:12:08Z — service=embeddings-router, symptom=503 spikes, p95 latency up. Severity: P2.

Ravi (oncall): Timeline notes — 03:11 UTC first uptick in 503s, 03:14 autoscaler launched 3 nodes, 03:17 one new node hit OOM during GC and was killed (kube node report attached), 03:20 I disabled aggressive scale-down and pinned 6 nodes, 03:25 rolled fallback to quantized v2-fallback which served requests with acceptable quality, 03:28 rates normalized. Total error volume ~0.3% of requests during window.

Jules (sre): Thanks — taking primary until 12:00 UTC. Current immediate status: embeddings-router stable, autoscaler set to conservative thresholds (min=4, max=12, cooldown=600s). I'm going to keep the pinned quantized fallback active for the next 2 hours while we observe.

Keisha (platform): I'm secondary. I'll follow up on the node OOM root cause and check kernel/oom-killer logs. Quick note: cloud image had a recent libc bump — pulling kernel logs now.

Marta (support): Customer impact: CS reported a handful of customers saw 503s (notably Acme Corp — ~120 failed requests total). I messaged Acme with an incident note template and offered a mitigation update. No paid-SLA breach expected but we should include counts in postmortem.

Jules (sre): Action items I'm taking now:
- keep cluster pinned at 6 nodes for 2 hours
- collect heapdump from the worker that OOMed (if available)
- run stacktrace sampling against the router for 30m to rule out hot-loop

Keisha (platform): My follow-ups:
- download /var/log/kern.log and kubelet logs from the OOM node ID=node-45
- validate VM host metrics (disk, memory, OOM events)
- open infra ticket RINF-742 with logs attached

Ravi (oncall): Runbook pointers for whoever picks this up:
- Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-router
- Quick commands I ran:
```bash
# graceful restart of the router deployment
kubectl -n embeddings rollout restart deploy/emb-router
# pin autoscaler min/max
kubectl -n infra apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: autoscaler-config
data:
  min_nodes: "4"
  max_nodes: "12"
  cooldown_s: "600"
EOF
# fallback switch (application flag)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/services/embeddings/switch-fallback?v=quantized-v2
```

Jules (sre): Coverage notes — Keisha, there's a small coverage gap for US-WEST between 05:00-07:00 UTC because team bandwidth is low; recommend we ask infra to temporarily increase reserved capacity if traffic expected. Marking as follow-up.

Keisha (platform): Ack. I'll also add a scheduled warm-up job for the pool to avoid cold startups during peak windows.

Marta (support): I'm opening an incident summary in Zendesk for the affected customers and linking the internal ticket. Template used: "Short outage window 03:11-03:28 UTC, 503 rate spike, mitigation applied: pinned nodes + quantized fallback. Next steps: postmortem if >30m, infra RCA."

Jules (sre): If this stays quiet for 2h I'll demote to monitoring-only and hand back. If we see repeat 503s, we escalate to P1 and start the full bridge.

Ravi (oncall): Passing primary to Jules. Remaining notes: logs bucket path gs://r-infra-logs/2026-03-14/embeddings/1848888888/, heapdump candidate file: worker-45-oom-heap-20260314.tar.gz.

incident-bot: Reminder: add timeline and customer impact to incident tracking ticket RINF-742 (auto-created).

Jules (sre): A couple more short-term items for follow-up list (assigning to Keisha/Ravi in RINF-742):
- attach kernel logs + kubelet logs from node-45
- confirm if GC configuration changed in last deploy (check commit 9f3a2b)
- run synthetic warmup for quantized-fallback to validate quality and latency

Keisha (platform): Noted — will attach logs and check CI release notes for commit 9f3a2b.

Marta (support): I'll update customers at 07:00 UTC with final counts and link to the handoff.

Jules (sre): Handoff complete — primary: Jules (until 12:00 UTC), secondary: Keisha. Coverage gap flagged for US-WEST 05:00-07:00 UTC. Runbook link again: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-router — see section "autoscaler churn".

Ravi (oncall): Thanks all — leaving the channel. :wave:
